native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among respondents ever flagged as incarcerated (ever_jailed=1, jailed 1985-1994, n=289 = 2.4%), 1985 median wealth (composite_wealth_1985) is near the floor of the distribution for everyone - $720 vs $3,600 for never-jailed respondents (20% of their level), with 39.4% holding exactly $0 - and the disparity that organises it runs incarceration status first, sex second, and race a weak third. Within race x sex cells, later jail is associated with a median wealth shortfall of $4,300 among Hispanic men ($700 vs $5,000; ratio 0.14; MWU p=0.00012, Cliff's delta -0.32) and $3,500 among white men ($2,000 vs $5,500; ratio 0.36; p=0.029, delta -0.17), but only $700 among Black men ($800 vs $1,500; ratio 0.53; p=0.082, delta -0.09, CI touching zero). Because never-jailed Black men already hold $1,500 - less than the $2,000 held by jailed white men - the floor reached by incarcerated respondents of every race ($700-$2,000) is compressed enough that race ordering within the incarcerated group is not resolvable (Black vs white jailed men -$1,200, 95% CI -$4,680 to +$600, p=0.15; Hispanic vs white -$1,300, CI -$5,000 to +$1,400, p=0.19; Black vs Hispanic +$100, p=0.87), while the sex axis inside the incarcerated group does separate: pooled jailed women (n=37) have median $0 vs $1,000 for pooled jailed men (n=252) (gap -$1,000, CI -$1,400 to -$260, p=0.024, delta -0.22). That sex gap reflects zero-dominance rather than debt: 64.9% of jailed women report exactly $0, rising to 81.2% of jailed Black women (n=16) and 77.8% of jailed Hispanic women (n=9), cells whose medians are structurally pinned at 0 and must not be read as magnitudes. The incarceration shortfall is not a bottom-only artifact: median deficits widen monotonically up the distribution (p25 $0, p50 -$2,880, p75 -$10,100, p90 -$49,610) while relative ratios stay flat (0.20-0.37), i.e. a multiplicative compression of wealth, and it widens after 1985 (overall gap -$2,880 in 1985, -$10,500 in 1990, -$8,500 in 1996, jailed medians $0 in every race cell by 1990). Framing: 1985 wealth is measured at or before most jail spells, so this is a prospective association - low 1985 wealth as a precursor marker of later jail, not a causal effect of incarceration on 1985 wealth. Because jail is self-reported (understating exposure and biasing contrasts toward the null) and the extract contains no survey weights, covariates, or residence/group-quarters field to identify incarceration any other way, these magnitudes are descriptive lower bounds.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Integrity check of data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013x6, zero nulls, race={black,hipanic[raw misspelling of Hispanic],white}, sex={female,male}, ever_jailed={0,1} with 289 ones). 2) Defined target subgroup ever_jailed==1 (n=289) with ever_jailed==0 (n=11,724) as reference; retained zeros (26.7% overall) and negatives (5.4%) in composite_wealth_1985 as substantive net-wealth values; no log transform, no winsorising in headline estimates; 'hipanic' kept internally with display mapping only. 3) Computed median + stratified percentile bootstrap 95% CI (B=10,000, seed 20261023) plus n, share-zero, share-negative, mean, p25, p75 for all 12 race x sex cells in both exposure groups (table1). 4) Primary lens: within-race within-sex incarcerated-minus-not-incarcerated dollar gaps and ratios with bootstrap CIs recomputed jointly on both strata in every replicate, plus Mann-Whitney U p-values and Cliff's delta and the fraction of replicates with jailed<not (table2, table2b). 5) Race contrasts at matched sex inside the incarcerated group, plus the pooled jailed-women (n=37) vs jailed-men (n=252) sex contrast (table3); female race cells reported descriptively with THIN n<20 / median-pinned-at-0 flags and used only as evidence of zero-dominance. 6) Robustness: mean-vs-median and p25/p75 split (no evidence the pattern is tail-driven; means rank identically), zero-floor and top-1%-winsorised (cut $273,949) medians (identical gaps), de-duplication sensitivity (1,899 rows and 50 jailed respondents dropped; no flip in headline gaps, one flip in a null within-jailed race contrast) (tables 4, 5, 7). 7) Secondary context only: 1990 and 1996 replication showing the gap widens (table6). 8) Wrote hypothesis naming specific strata, directions and CIs, with explicit prospective/non-causal framing and the caveat that the jail-as-place-of-enumeration proxy is unavailable in this file.

sub_hypo.context: Individuals who were ever incarcerated (ever_jailed = 1), with wealth measured in 1985.
sub_hypo.relations: Males have higher median wealth in 1985 than females.

sub_hypo.text: Respondents jailed during 1985–1994 have near-floor 1985 median wealth of $720 versus $3,600 among never-jailed respondents, a $2,880 deficit and a ratio of 0.20; 39.4% of jailed respondents hold exactly $0.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort extract: 12,013 respondents, including 289 ever-jailed respondents (2.4%) and 11,724 never-jailed respondents. Zeros and negative net wealth are retained. Wealth in 1985 is measured at or before most jail spells, making this a prospective, non-causal association. Self-reported jail exposure and the absence of survey weights, covariates, and residence/group-quarters information limit the estimates to descriptive lower bounds as framed in the hypothesis.
sub_hypo.relations: Low 1985 wealth is a precursor marker of later reported incarceration, not an estimated causal effect of incarceration on 1985 wealth.

sub_hypo.text: The 1985 wealth disparity is organized primarily by incarceration status, secondarily by sex, and only weakly by race within the incarcerated group.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY1979 cohort extract; comparisons across incarceration groups within race-by-sex cells, matched-sex race contrasts among jailed respondents, and pooled sex contrasts among jailed respondents.
sub_hypo.relations: Incarceration status is the primary axis of wealth disparity; sex separates wealth within the jailed group, whereas within-jailed race ordering is not statistically resolvable.

sub_hypo.text: Among Hispanic men, later jail is associated with 1985 median wealth of $700 versus $5,000 for never-jailed men: a $4,300 shortfall, ratio 0.14, Mann–Whitney U p=0.00012, and Cliff's delta −0.32.
sub_hypo.context: Hispanic male respondents in the NLSY1979 cohort extract, comparing ever_jailed=1 with ever_jailed=0; the raw race label 'hipanic' is displayed as Hispanic.
sub_hypo.relations: Within Hispanic men, later incarceration is prospectively associated with substantially lower 1985 wealth.

sub_hypo.text: Among white men, later jail is associated with 1985 median wealth of $2,000 versus $5,500 for never-jailed men: a $3,500 shortfall, ratio 0.36, p=0.029, and Cliff's delta −0.17.
sub_hypo.context: White male respondents in the NLSY1979 cohort extract, comparing ever_jailed=1 with ever_jailed=0.
sub_hypo.relations: Within white men, later incarceration is prospectively associated with lower 1985 wealth.

sub_hypo.text: Among Black men, later jail is associated with 1985 median wealth of $800 versus $1,500 for never-jailed men: a $700 shortfall, ratio 0.53, p=0.082, and Cliff's delta −0.09, with a confidence interval touching zero.
sub_hypo.context: Black male respondents in the NLSY1979 cohort extract, comparing ever_jailed=1 with ever_jailed=0.
sub_hypo.relations: Within Black men, the prospective incarceration-associated median shortfall is smaller than among Hispanic or white men, with uncertainty touching zero.

sub_hypo.text: Never-jailed Black men have lower 1985 median wealth ($1,500) than jailed white men ($2,000). sub_hypo.context: Male respondents in the NLSY1979 cohort extract; cross-status Black–white comparison and matched-sex race comparisons restricted to ever_jailed=1.
sub_hypo.relations: Low baseline wealth among never-jailed Black men coexists with compressed, statistically unresolved racial wealth differences among jailed men.

sub_hypo.text: Among jailed respondents pooled across races, women (n=37) have 1985 median wealth of $0 versus $1,000 for men (n=252): a −$1,000 gap, 95% CI −$1,400 to −$260, p=0.024, and Cliff's delta −0.22.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY1979 cohort respondents with ever_jailed=1, comparing women with men pooled across race.
sub_hypo.relations: Within the jailed group, women have lower 1985 wealth than men, with a median-gap confidence interval excluding zero.

sub_hypo.text: The sex gap among jailed respondents reflects zero-dominance rather than debt: 64.9% of jailed women report exactly $0 in 1985 wealth, including 81.2% of jailed Black women (n=16) and 77.8% of jailed Hispanic women (n=9). These small female race cells have medians structurally pinned at zero and must not be interpreted as magnitudes.
sub_hypo.context: Female NLSY1979 cohort respondents with ever_jailed=1; Black and Hispanic female cells have fewer than 20 respondents and are used descriptively as evidence of zero-dominance.
sub_hypo.relations: A majority holding exactly zero wealth pins jailed women's subgroup medians at zero; the sex disparity is attributed to zero concentration rather than negative wealth.

sub_hypo.text: The incarceration-associated wealth shortfall is not confined to the bottom: jailed-minus-never-jailed quantile gaps widen monotonically from $0 at p25 to −$2,880 at p50, −$10,100 at p75, and −$49,610 at p90, while relative ratios remain approximately flat at 0.20–0.37.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY1979 cohort extract, comparing the 1985 wealth distributions of ever-jailed and never-jailed respondents with zeros and negatives retained and no headline log transformation or winsorization.
sub_hypo.relations: Increasing absolute deficits across wealth quantiles alongside approximately stable relative ratios indicate multiplicative wealth compression rather than a bottom-only artifact.

sub_hypo.text: The overall jailed-minus-never-jailed median wealth gap is larger after 1985: −$2,880 in 1985, −$10,500 in 1990, and −$8,500 in 1996. By 1990, jailed respondents have median wealth of $0 in every race cell.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY1979 cohort extract using the same ever_jailed indicator for jail during 1985–1994; 1990 and 1996 comparisons provide secondary context.
sub_hypo.relations: The absolute median wealth deficit is greater in both later years than in 1985, though smaller in 1996 than in 1990; jailed racial groups reach zero median wealth by 1990.
